target_customer: Hospitals and diagnostic imaging centres in emerging markets
problem: Many facilities in emerging markets lack radiologists, reliable internet and electricity, so scans go unread or are read slowly.
business_model: Teleradiology services plus cloud PACS software and edge hardware sold to imaging facilities
product_category: Teleradiology and medical imaging software and hardware

founders.name: Aschkan Abdul-Malek
founders.background_notes: CEO per later profiles; YC page lists him as Founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Medical imaging gateways, cloud PACS and AI reading support are standard but regulated engineering, with edge hardware for poor connectivity.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with imaging devices and a radiologist network help, but no strong lock in found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents acting; the company still operates.

market_need_then: Radiologist shortages in emerging markets are documented widely, but no dated source was opened for 2017.

identity.voice_and_tone: Corporate healthcare technology; tagline Transforming teleradiology for a connected world

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; product names AlemBox and AlemHub extend the name.

pivots.from: AI radiologist in a box hardware and software
pivots.to: Teleradiology network with cloud PACS, RIS and AI assisted reporting
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from YC page versus current site wording only

outcome_analysis: AlemHealth survives as a Singapore based teleradiology and imaging software company that claims 5M plus studies a year across 40 plus countries, all self reported. No acquisition, shutdown or credible funding beyond a tiny 2017 seed was found, so its trajectory is unclear. A later profile notes no FDA clearance or publications, which limits independent validation.
notes: A 2017 seed of about 120K USD appears only on aggregators (CB Insights, Seedtable) with totals from 85K to 210K, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. No 2017 competitor source was opened; Zebra Medical Vision and Qure.ai surfaced only in later aggregator material. Founding year not found; the YC page does not state it. Founder roles come from aggregator profiles. Nothing found that explains the name.
